I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Trenggalek Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Trenggalek Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Trenggalek.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Trenggalek Regency.
5. Implementation is the form of execution of protection of women and children including protection of women and children victims of violence.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.
10. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
12. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (drugs) abuse, children victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children victims of abuse and neglect.
13. Protection of Women and Children Victims of violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
14. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development policies and programs.
15. Child rights mainstreaming is a strategy to integrate child issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policies, programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child.
16. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
17. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development properly.
18. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent.
19. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of parental authority, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination.
20. Foster child is a child who is cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because their parents or one of their parents is unable to guarantee the child's proper growth and development.
21. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop children in accordance with their religion and abilities, talents, and interests.
22. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
26. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
27. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a parent over a child.
28. Every person is an individual or corporation.
29. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children (PPTPA) is a network of cooperation that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
30. Safe House (Shelter) is a shelter for women and children including families and witnesses of violence victims.
31. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
32. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
33. Criminal Act of Human Trafficking is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of a criminal act determined in the Law on Human Trafficking.

Article 64

1. Families and communities are obligated to prevent the occurrence of violence and the occurrence of criminal acts against women and children.
2. Every person who hears, sees, or knows of the occurrence of violence is obligated to make efforts in accordance with their capabilities to:
a. prevent the continuation of criminal acts;
b. provide protection to victims;
c. provide emergency assistance; and
d. assist in the process of submitting applications for protection orders.

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of the protection of women and children including the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 54

1. Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 44 includes physical, psychological, and sexual violence carried out through efforts to:
a. disseminate and socialize the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitor, report, and impose sanctions.
2. Everyone is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 3

The objectives of implementing protection of women are:
a. to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. to protect women and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women; and
c. to maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

Article 65

1. The community participates in assisting efforts to prevent and handle victims of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting the existence of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children to law enforcement or authorities, or participating in handling victims of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children.
3. To implement the participation as referred to in paragraph (2), the community is entitled to obtain legal protection.
4. The Regional Government in providing victim protection may cooperate with the community or social community institutions.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TRENGGALEK REGENCY

NUMBER 10 OF 2012

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF TRENGGALEK,

Considering:

a. that the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees the welfare of each of its citizens, including protection of women's rights and children's rights which are human rights; b. that in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women is an effort to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life; c. that every child is a bud, potential, and the next generation of the nation's struggle, and is expected to be able to bear such responsibility in the future, therefore they need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally and socially, and have noble character, so that protection efforts need to be made and to realize child welfare by providing guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and treatment without discrimination; d. that violence against women and children is a crime against humanity which constitutes a violation of human rights; e. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, letter c, and letter d, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children; In View of:

This provision is intended to give freedom to children in order to develop their creativity and intellectuality (reasoning ability) in accordance with the child's age level. The provisions of this article also affirm that such development must still be under the guidance of their parents.

Point d
The provision regarding the right of the child to know who their parents are, in the sense of their origins (including their wet nurse), is intended to avoid the severance of lineage and blood relations between the child and their biological parents, while the right to be raised and cared for by their parents is intended so that the child can obey and respect their parents.

Point e

Point i
Discriminatory treatment, for example treatment that differentiates ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status of the child, birth order of the child, and physical and/or mental condition.

Exploitative treatment, for example actions or conduct that instrumentalizes, utilizes, or exploits children to obtain personal, family, or group benefits. Neglectful treatment, for example actions or conduct that deliberately ignores the obligation to maintain, care for, or look after the child as appropriate.

Cruel treatment, for example actions or conduct that is tyrannical, vicious, brutal, or shows no compassion toward the child.

Violent and abusive treatment, for example conduct that injures and/or harms the child, and not merely physical, but also mental and social.

Unjust treatment, for example actions of partiality between one child and another, or arbitrariness toward the child.

Other wrongful treatment, for example actions of harassment or indecent conduct toward the child.

Point j
What is meant by "separation" is not eliminating the relationship of the child with their parents.

Point k
What is meant by "protection" includes activities that are direct and indirect in nature, from actions that endanger the child physically and psychologically.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Part One

Rights of Victims

Article 56

1. Special protection for child victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 44 shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by the Regional Government and the community.
2. Everyone is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering to involve children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 44

Regional Governments and other state institutions are obliged and responsible for providing special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect.

Article 51

1. Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 44 is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and the community.
2. Special protection for children who are exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
a. dissemination and/or socialization of the provisions of Laws and Regulations relating to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various Regional Government agencies, companies, labor unions, Community Social Institutions, and the community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of children.
3. Everyone is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in the exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 12

1. Every child who is deprived of liberty has the right to:
a. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal proceedings; and
c. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
2. Every child who is a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

Article 62

The Regional Government is obligated to implement prevention of acts of violence, criminal acts of trafficking in persons, and protection efforts for victims.

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. 26. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
27. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a parent over a child.
28. Every person is an individual or corporation.
29. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children (PPTPA) is a network of cooperation that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
30. Safe House (Shelter) is a shelter for women and children including families and witnesses of violence victims.
31. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations.
32. Human Trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
33. Criminal Act of Human Trafficking is any act or series of acts that meet the elements of a criminal act determined in the Law on Human Trafficking.

Article 54

1. Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 44 includes physical, psychological, and sexual violence carried out through efforts to:
a. disseminate and socialize the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitor, report, and impose sanctions.
2. Everyone is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

Article 3

The objectives of implementing protection of women are:
a. to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. to protect women and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women; and
c. to maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of the protection of women and children including the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of the protection of women and children including the protection of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

Article 54

1. Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 44 includes physical, psychological, and sexual violence carried out through efforts to:
a. disseminate and socialize the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitor, report, and impose sanctions.
2. Everyone is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering to commit, or participating in violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of the protection of women and children including the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 3

The objectives of implementing protection of women are:
a. to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. to protect women and prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women; and
c. to maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

Article 62

The Regional Government is obligated to implement prevention of acts of violence, criminal acts of trafficking in persons, and protection efforts for victims.

I. GENERAL

The existence of Regional Regulations that favor vulnerable or subordinated groups, particularly women and children, is urgently needed in connection with the many social problems that result in the deprivation of the human rights of women and children. The human rights of women and children are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child as well as the ratification of the convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, however the enforcement of the human rights of women and children has still not been able to encourage political commitment in the Region. The form of implementation of women's protection carried out by the Government is to implement gender mainstreaming, namely a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of Regional development program policies within the framework of National development. Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms. Although Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection has included the rights of children, the implementation of the obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state to provide protection to children, a Regional Regulation is still needed as a juridical basis for the implementation of these obligations and responsibilities in the Region. Thus, the formation of this Regional Regulation is based on the consideration that child protection in all its aspects is part of development activities in the Region, particularly in advancing national and state life. Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

Likewise, in the context of implementing child protection, the state and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their optimal and directed growth and development. This Regional Regulation affirms that the responsibility of parents, families, communities, Regional Government and the state is a series of activities carried out continuously for the protection of children's rights. This series of activities must be sustainable and directed to ensure the growth and development of children, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially. This action is intended to realize the best life for children who are expected to be potential successors to the nation, resilient, having nationalism imbued with noble character and Pancasila values, and having a strong will to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. Child protection efforts need to be implemented as early as possible, namely from the fetus in the womb until the child is 18 (eighteen) years old. Starting from the concept of comprehensive, complete, and comprehensive child protection, this Regional Regulation places the obligation to provide protection to children based on the following principles:
a. non-discrimination; b. the best interests of the child; c. the right to life, survival, and development; and d. respect for the views of the child. In conducting guidance, development and protection of children, the role of the community is needed, whether through child protection institutions, religious institutions, non-governmental organizations, community organizations, social organizations, business world, mass media, or educational institutions. The form of implementation of child protection carried out by the Regional Government is through mainstreaming children's rights, namely integrating children's issues and rights into every stage of development which includes planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of legislation, policy programs, activities and budgets with the principles of the best interests of the child. The integrity and harmony of a happy, safe, peaceful and tranquil household is the aspiration of everyone in the household. The Republic of Indonesia is a state based on Belief in the One and Only God guaranteed by Article 29 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Thus, every person within the household in exercising their rights and obligations must be based on religion. This needs to be continuously developed in order to build household integrity. To realize this integrity and harmony, it is highly dependent on each person within the household, especially the quality level of behavior and self-control of each person within the household. Household integrity and harmony can be disrupted if quality and self-control cannot be controlled, which ultimately can lead to domestic violence resulting in insecurity or injustice towards people within the household. To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, the state and society are obliged to carry out prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the Pancasila philosophy and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state views that all forms of violence, especially domestic violence, are violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination. The state's view is based on Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, along with - 42 - its amendments.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

Rights and Obligations of Women

Article 64

1. Families and communities are obligated to prevent the occurrence of violence and the occurrence of criminal acts against women and children.
2. Every person who hears, sees, or knows of the occurrence of violence is obligated to make efforts in accordance with their capabilities to:
a. prevent the continuation of criminal acts;
b. provide protection to victims;
c. provide emergency assistance; and
d. assist in the process of submitting applications for protection orders.

Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something that is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person has the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice". Current developments show that acts of physical, psychological, sexual violence, and household neglect in reality occur so that adequate legal instruments are needed to eliminate domestic violence. The Regional Regulation regulates the prevention and protection as well as recovery of victims of violence, and regulates the obligations of law enforcement officers, health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, or spiritual counselors to protect victims so that they are more sensitive and responsive to household interests which from the outset are directed towards household integrity and harmony. To prevent domestic violence, the Regional Government is obliged to carry out tasks in the field of women's empowerment to carry out preventive actions, among others, organizing communication, information, and education on the prevention of violence against women and children. Based on these considerations, it is time to establish a Regional Regulation that is regulated comprehensively, clearly, and firmly in the implementation of the protection of women and children including the protection of women and children victims of violence.

Article 65

1. The community participates in assisting efforts to prevent and handle victims of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting the existence of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children to law enforcement or authorities, or participating in handling victims of violence as well as criminal acts against women and children.
3. To implement the participation as referred to in paragraph (2), the community is entitled to obtain legal protection.
4. The Regional Government in providing victim protection may cooperate with the community or social community institutions.
